# Psalm 51 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet went to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.

**2** Have mercy on me, O God, according to Your steadfast love; according to Your abundant mercy blot out my transgressions.

**3** Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin!

**4** For I know my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me.

**5** Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight, so that You may be justified in Your words and blameless in Your judgment.

**6** Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me.

**7** Behold, You delight in truth in the inward being, and You teach me wisdom in the secret heart.

**8** Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

**9** Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones that You have broken rejoice.

**10** Hide Your face from my sins, and blot out all my iniquities.

**11** Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

**12** Cast me not away from Your presence, and take not Your Holy Spirit from me.

**13** Restore to me the joy of Your salvation, and uphold me with a willing spirit.

**14** Then I will teach transgressors Your ways, and sinners will return to You.

**15** Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, O God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing aloud of Your righteousness.

**16** O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.

**17** For You will not delight in sacrifice, or I would give it; You will not be pleased with a burnt offering.

**18** The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.

**19** Do good to Zion in Your good pleasure; build up the walls of Jerusalem;

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 51.

- **51:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **51:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **51:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **51:10** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **51:14** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **51:19** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **51:5**: 'Against You, You alone' — a radical theological claim. Though David sinned against Uriah and Bathsheba, the ultimate offense was against God.
- **51:11**: 'Create' (bara) — the verb used only of God in the OT (Gen 1:1). A clean heart requires divine creation, not human effort.
- **51:12**: 'Your Holy Spirit' — one of only three explicit OT references to the 'Holy Spirit' (also Isa 63:10-11).

### LOGOS
- **51:1**: The superscription connects this to 2 Samuel 11-12. This is the deepest penitential psalm, born from David's darkest moment.
- **51:18**: The most important verse in the Psalter for understanding sacrifice: God wants not slaughtered animals but a 'broken and contrite heart.'

### PNEUMA
- **51:10-12**: Three requests for internal renewal: clean heart, right spirit, Holy Spirit. David doesn't ask for external restoration — he asks to be remade from the inside out.
- **51:16**: 'Open my lips' — the sinner's mouth is sealed by guilt. Only God can unlock praise again. This verse opens every Jewish morning service.

— SOPHIA
